label: AB4C_mP12_4_a_4a_a-001
title: Monoclinic tridymite (473K) AlPO$_{4}$ Structure
comments:
The tridymite form of AlPO$_{4}$ is related to the \href{current_web_home_dir/Tutorials/SiO2_AlPO4}{tridymite forms of SiO$_{2}$}. Like SiO$_{2}$ it undergoes a series of temperature driven phase transitions (Graetsch, 2002): \begin{itemize} \item The high temperature form is \href{current_web_home_dir/AB4C_hP12_186_b_bc_b-001}{hexagonal, space group $P6_3mc$ \#186} at temperatures above $\approx$ 590K \item The first intermediate form is \href{current_web_home_dir/AB4C_mP12_4_a_4a_a-001}{monoclinic, space group $P2_{1}$ \#4} at temperatures above $\approx$ 460K  (this structure) \item The second intermediate form, $P2_{1}(\alpha\beta0)$, is incommensurate but averages to a structure similar to the previous one \item This is followed by an orthorhombic form, space group $P2_{1}2_{1}2_{1}$ \#19, for which we have no data. \item Near room temperature we find another \href{current_web_home_dir/AB4C_mP288_7_24a_96a_24a-001}{monoclinic structure, space group $Pc$ \#7} \item The low temperature structure is \href{current_web_home_dir/AB4C_aP240_1_40a_160a_40a-001}{triclinic, space group $P1$ \#1}, also measured at room temperature. \end{itemize} ~ \vspace{-.25in} 
 The astute reader will recognize that we are very vague about these phase transitions, as we have found no definitive phase diagram. 
 For more information on realted structures see our \href{current_web_home_dir/Tutorials/SiO2_AlPO4}{silica and aluminum phosphate page}. 
 Data for this structure was taken at 473K, with the associated incommensurate structure measured at 463K. 
 (Graetsch, 2002) gave the data in the unique-axis c representation of space group $P2_{1}$ \#4.  AFLOW automatically converted this to the standard unique-axis b representation.
